data.name: Sharukh
data.gender_notes: Sharukh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is radiant and a king, derived from the Sanskrit words 'sharu' meaning king and 'ruk' meaning radiance. The name Sharukh carries the meaning “King, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sharukh usually hope their child will grow to embody king, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the inner radiance and power of an individual, evoking feelings of courage, confidence, and leadership.
data.etymology: Sharukh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharukh total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sharukh carries a rich cultural heritage in the Indian subcontinent, particularly among the Hindus. The name evokes the sense of power, royalty, and strength, reflecting the deep-rooted traditions of the Indian culture. It is a name that inspires respect and awe, evoking images of brave rulers who defended their kingdoms against all odds. This cultural significance extends to the realm of entertainment, with Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan adding another layer to the name's meaning as a charismatic and influential "king of hearts."
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Sharukh lies in its innate connection to divine royalty and radiance. In Hindu mythology, gods and goddesses are often depicted as kings and queens of the divine realm. Sharukh is a reminder of the inner spiritual king or queen that each individual possesses, the innate radiance of the soul that can shine brightly, and the inner strength that enables us to rule over our thoughts and emotions. The name encourages us to embrace our inner royalty, tap into our inner radiance, and lead a life of excellence and purpose.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sharukh in Hinduism symbolizes the radiant and shining king within an individual. It signifies the inner strength and power that every person holds, encouraging them to embrace their royal status and rule over their own lives with courage and dignity.

historical_references.reference: Shahanshah Shahab-ud-Din Muhammad Khurdadiot Shah, popularly known as Shahrukh, ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1401 to 1445. He was a Turko-Afghan king who extended the Timurid Empire in India.
historical_references.context: Medieval India, Delhi Sultanate, Timurid Empire

historical_references.reference: Sharukh, another name for the legendary king Rama, is mentioned in the epic Ramayana. He is the father of Sita, the beloved wife of Lord Rama, and the king of Videha.

modern_usage.modern_context: Sharukh Khan, commonly known as SRK or King Khan, is a renowned Bollywood actor popularly recognized for his romantic roles. He has a significant presence on social media platforms such as Instagram, Twitter, and YouTube. On Instagram, he shares glimpses of his personal life, professional projects, and philanthropy work. He has over 73 million followers. Twitter is another platform where he frequently interacts with fans, shares his views on various topics, and promotes his upcoming films. His Twitter account has over 38 million followers. Lastly, on YouTube, his music videos, interviews, and film trailers receive millions of views. The modern context shows that Sharukh Khan leverages these platforms to engage with fans, promote his work, and maintain a strong online presence.
